claims.text: The 60-second apnea window starting at 2000-01-03T04:47:00+00:00 (window index 287) was classified as normal by the detector.

The detector's reconstruction error was 1.3989, well below the anomaly threshold of 190.87, yielding a normalized margin of -0.9927; the detector's semantics are reconstruction threshold evidence, not probability or calibrated confidence.

The model is a BiLSTM temporal-attention autoencoder (version apnea-03-a03_seed2026) trained on the apnea dataset and tested on patient a03; no signal-level or attention-level evidence was available for this window.
In the five preceding windows (04:42 to 04:46), all predictions were normal with reconstruction errors between 1.32 and 1.40, and no anomalies were recorded.
Across the 12 most recent 5-minute buckets (03:50 to 04:45), the mean reconstruction error increased from 1.141 to 1.349, with zero anomalies in every bucket.
Over the 287 windows analyzed before 04:47, the anomaly rate was 0.0% and the mean reconstruction error was 1.581, with a maximum reconstruction error of 72.42.

The patient has a suspected diagnosis of sleep-disordered breathing (R06.83) from a sleep consultation on 1999-12-15, with notes of loud snoring and daytime fatigue; this is a synthetic prototype and not an official PhysioNet diagnosis.
